sir,
    Sir we r conduct Indian peafowl data in our university campus, year 2015 and 2016, by using line transect sampling method. Our assumption is that most of the object detected in transect line so histogram is graph is negative exponential type but here seen that most of the object detect in middle of the half width or the end of the width so we estimate f(mode) value instead of f(0) in the estimation formula also we use kernel density estimation. Can we make further correction????

Interesting thing is that the estimates of both the methods (frequency curve and kernel density) are not far away. Please suggest more information if??? And sorry for my English.

Thank u.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] About analysis of Indian Peafowl data.
parts:
Gajanan

Just because two estimates are close to each other does not imply they are correct.  From your description of the shape of your perpendicular distance histogram, it would seem that one of the assumptions of distance sampling is violated when the data were collected. 

Specifically, it seems that the peafowl were detecting the observers before the observers were detecting the peafowl.  As a consequence, the birds were moving away from the transect before they were detected.  The bump you see in your histogram is a result of this responsive movement on the part of the peafowl.  Section 11.4.2 of Buckland et al. (2015) discusses the problem of responsive movement.
